reason: Checks Playwright's runtime refusal of a string `state` option (`expected one of (attached|detached|visible|hidden)`) and of a `visibility` option, with its migration hint. Strider has no state option: each state is its own matcher (`Expect.toBeAttached`, `toBeDetached`, `toBeVisible`, `toBeHidden`), so a wrong state doesn't compile, and there is no string to refuse at run time

Uses Playwright's internal `__testHookBeforeAdoptNode`, which runs between finding a node and adopting it into the page's world, and its `mode` fixture, which these tests skip outside the default mode. Strider has no adoption step to hook

decision: Playwright is evidence, not the template
reason: Waits for a selector inside a handle whose element is then removed, and expects the wait to throw 'Element is not attached to the DOM'. Strider has no handle bound to one element: a locator inside a button re-resolves on each attempt, so when the button is removed the wait keeps looking rather than throwing

Waits for an XPath selector whose evaluation is the point: WA-065 selects a paragraph by `normalize-space(.)`, and WA-070 an element by an absolute path with a single slash, `//html/body/div`. Strider's locators take CSS, not XPath, so a CSS selector for the same element would pass without testing either. XPath is planned for 1.0
